newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan rupee ends at previous record low.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan rupee ends at previous record low.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee ended at its previous close of 56.90 to the dollar, also the previous record low, after moving in a tight range on Friday, dealers said.
"Movement was very tight from 56.87 to 56.90," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
Dealers said there were minor import deals and speculators were not active ahead of the weekend.
Many banks had also expected the Central Bank to push the rupee much lower against the dollar while it barely touched the U.S. unit despite its overseas losses, dealers said.
The Central Bank pushed down the dollar by only a quarter local cent and set buying and selling rates at 55.8954 and 57.0246.
The rupee opened at 56.85 to the dollar but there was no trading in the first several hours as the market searched for directon after closing at an all-time low of 56.90 on Thursday.
The overnight call money rate closed at 18.5 percent after opening at 17.5, dealers said.
